To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the locomotor-related activity in the isolated spinal cord reduces the concentration of extracellular calcium ([Cao]) and increases the concentration of extracular potassium ([Ko]), that such changes in [Cao] and [Ko] trigger pacemaker activities, and that the emergence of these pacemaker properties critically depends on a [Cao]-dependent activation of the persistent Na+ current (INa(P)).

activity-dependent changes in the extracellular concentrations of Ca2+ and of K+ trigger pacemaker activities of neurons considered to be part in the spinal locomotor network, and that this pacemaker activity critically depends on the activation of a persistent sodium current.
the extracellular calcium concentration decreases and the extracellular potassium concentration increases in the neonatal rodent isolated spinal cord during fictive locomotion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how the activity of large neuronal populations can be coordinated.
the generation of rhythmic locomotor-like activity and its underlying mechanisms in the isolated spinal cord of neonatal rodents (rats and mice).
the question of how the activity-dependent changes of the extracellular ion concentrations ([Ca2+]o, [K+]o) influence the properties of neurons in the isolated spinal cord of neonatal mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
activity-dependent changes in the extracellular concentrations of calcium ([Ca2+]) and potassium ([K+]) can trigger pacemaker activities that are critical for locomotion in the spinal cord.
changes in the extracellular ion concentration can be a trigger of pacemakers in neurons that are part of the spinal locomotor-related circuit.
the activity-dependent changes of extracellular calcium and potassium in the spinal cord are important to tune the properties of interneurons and thus the network activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
activity-dependent changes in the extracellular Ca2+ concentration ([Ca(2+)o]) and K+ concentration ([K+]o) trigger the emergence of pacemakers in the spinal locomotor network.
activity-dependent changes in the extracellular ion concentrations are an essential part of the locomotion control system.
the activity-dependent changes in the ionic milieu of the spinal cord are sufficient to generate pacemaker activities in the locomotor network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the extracellular  ionic environment can be an important determinant of the intrinsic activity of individual neurons and of the operation of neuronal circuits.
the changes in [Ca2+]o and [K+]o induced by neuronal firing activity may be a critical component of neuronal and network function.

activity-dependent changes in extracellular ion concentrations are a natural consequence of neuronal network activity and that they can trigger pacemaker properties in neurons that are part of the network.
